processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Applied to the Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C-(0,3)Cu austenitic low-density steels (0Cu steel or 3Cu steel) as the first step, before the aging treatment.
Aging treatment applied sequentially after solution treatment, producing the aged state of the 0Cu steel. In this state κ-carbide is able to precipitate from the austenitic matrix of the 0Cu steel.

structures.overall_structure: Austenitic (γ) matrix of the 0Cu Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C low-density steel from which intragranular κ-carbide is able to precipitate upon aging. The solution-treated lattice parameter of the 0Cu steel (a = 0.3687 nm) exceeds the critical lattice parameter (~0.3670 nm) and the Al content exceeds the critical Al content (6.52 wt%), so κ-carbide precipitation is enabled in this steel.

phases_present.crystal_structure: FCC (austenitic matrix; lattice parameter a = 0.3687 nm under solution treatment)

characterization_methods.purpose: Determination of the lattice parameter of the austenitic matrix of the 0Cu steel.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The lattice parameter of the 0Cu steel under solid solution treatment is a = 0.3687 nm, which is higher than the critical lattice parameter (~0.3670 nm), enabling κ-carbide precipitation.

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts the critical Al content required for intragranular κ-carbide precipitation in Fe-Mn-Al-C steel; applied to the 0Cu steel to yield a critical Al content of 6.52 wt%.

unmapped_findings: Lattice parameter of the 0Cu steel (Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C) under solution treatment is a = 0.3687 nm according to XRD calculations, compared with a = 0.3689 nm for the 3Cu steel.

The critical lattice parameter of the austenitic matrix for intragranular κ-carbide precipitation in Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is about a = 0.3670 nm; the 0Cu steel value (a = 0.3687 nm) is higher, so κ-carbide can precipitate from the 0Cu steel.

Using the composition boundary formula 0.208(wt.%C) + 0.098(wt.%Al) = 1 − 0.0054(wt.%Mn), the critical Al content for κ-carbide precipitation in the 0Cu steel is calculated to be 6.52 wt%; the Al content in the 0Cu steel exceeds 6.52 wt%, so κ-carbide has sufficient precipitation ability in this steel.
